question: How many elements are listed in the modern periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 118.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The modern periodic table currently lists 118 elements, with atomic numbers from 1 (Hydrogen) to 118 (Oganesson). (आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी में 118 तत्व)

• All 118 positions have been officially confirmed and named by the IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry); the last four (113 Nihonium, 115 Moscovium, 117 Tennessine, 118 Oganesson) were named in 2016.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Of the 118 elements, about 94 occur naturally and the rest are synthetic (man-made).

• The Modern Periodic Law was given by Henry Moseley (1913): "The physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers."

• Mendeleev's periodic law (1869) was based on atomic mass; he is called the Father of the Periodic Table.

NOTE

• The modern periodic table has 7 periods (horizontal rows) and 18 groups (vertical columns).

• Group 1 — alkali metals; Group 2 — alkaline earth metals; Group 17 — halogens; Group 18 — noble/inert gases.

question: In which of the following States was the third edition of Khelo India University Games held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The third edition of the Khelo India University Games (KIUG 2022) was held in Uttar Pradesh in May–June 2023, across Varanasi, Lucknow, Gorakhpur and Gautam Buddha Nagar (Noida), with the Rowing events at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. (खेलो इंडिया यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar topped the medal tally in this edition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Khelo India University Games editions: 1st — Odisha (Bhubaneswar, 2020), 2nd — Karnataka (Bengaluru, 2021 held in 2022), 3rd — Uttar Pradesh (2023), 4th — Guwahati, Assam (2024).

• The Khelo India programme was launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in 2018 to revive sports culture at the grassroots level.

NOTE

• Other Khelo India events: Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Winter Games (held in Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir) and Khelo India Para Games.

question: Which country did India beat in the final to win the 2023 Intercontinental Cup Football championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lebanon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India defeated Lebanon 2–0 in the final of the 2023 Intercontinental Cup football tournament, held at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar (Odisha) in June 2023. (इंटरकॉन्टिनेंटल कप 2023 — भारत ने लेबनान को हराया)

• Sunil Chhetri scored both goals in the final; he was also the top scorer of the tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other teams in the 2023 edition were Mongolia and Vanuatu.

• India, coached by Igor Stimac, went on to win the SAFF Championship 2023 as well in the same season.

• India had also won the first edition of the Intercontinental Cup in 2018 (Mumbai), beating Kenya.

NOTE

• Sunil Chhetri is India's most-capped player and highest goal-scorer, and among the highest active international goal-scorers in world football.

• Indian football's governing body is the All India Football Federation (AIFF), founded in 1937.

question: In which state of India is shifting cultivation known as Bringa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Odisha, the practice of shifting cultivation is locally known as "Bringa" (also spelt Biringa). (ओडिशा — स्थानांतरित कृषि "ब्रिंगा")

• Shifting cultivation ("slash-and-burn" agriculture) is a primitive farming method in which a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, crops are grown for a few years until the soil loses fertility, and the farmer then moves to a new patch.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Local names of shifting cultivation in India:

◦ Jhum — North-Eastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland).

◦ Podu / Penda — Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Odisha.

◦ Bewar, Mashan, Penda, Beera — Madhya Pradesh.

◦ Kumari — Western Ghats (Kerala).

◦ Khil — Himalayan belt; Dahiya — Bundelkhand; Kuruwa — Jharkhand.

• Outside India: Milpa (Mexico/Central America), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam), Chena (Sri Lanka), Roca (Brazil), Masole (Congo).

NOTE

• Shifting cultivation causes deforestation, soil erosion and loss of fertility, and hence governments discourage it and promote settled farming and horticulture instead.

question: What does the acronym ‘ATM’ stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Automated Teller Machine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "ATM" stands for "Automated Teller Machine" — an electronic banking outlet that allows customers to complete basic transactions (cash withdrawal, deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, PIN change, fund transfer) without the help of a bank teller. (स्वचालित टेलर मशीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The world's first ATM was installed by Barclays Bank in London (1967); its invention is credited to John Shepherd-Barron (who was born in Shillong, India).

• The first ATM in India was set up by HSBC in Mumbai in 1987.

• White Label ATMs (WLAs) are owned and operated by non-bank entities (e.g., Tata Indicash); Brown Label ATMs are owned by a service provider but the cash and network belong to a bank.

NOTE

• Other banking abbreviations: NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer), RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement), IMPS (Immediate Payment Service), UPI (Unified Payments Interface), KYC (Know Your Customer), IFSC (Indian Financial System Code).

question: Who had founded the first Women’s University in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhondo Keshav Karve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dhondo Keshav Karve (popularly called Maharshi Karve) founded India's first Women's University in 1916 at Pune, later known as the Shreemati Nathibai Damodar Thackersey (SNDT) Women's University (its headquarters shifted to Mumbai). (महर्षि धोंडो केशव कर्वे — प्रथम महिला विश्वविद्यालय, 1916)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Karve was a great social reformer who worked for widow remarriage and women's education. He established the Widow Marriage Association (1893) and the Hindu Widows' Home at Hingne, Pune (1896); he himself married a widow.

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1958, on his 100th birthday.

NOTE

• Other reformers linked with women's education: Jyotiba Phule and Savitribai Phule (first girls' school, Pune, 1848), Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (widow remarriage, Widow Remarriage Act 1856), Raja Ram Mohan Roy (abolition of Sati, 1829).

• Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh (1875) — later AMU; Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee was a legendary Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta; W. W. Hunter headed the Hunter Commission (1882) on education.

question: Devendra Jhajharia won which medal/place in World Para Athletics Grand Prix?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Silver.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian para-athlete Devendra Jhajharia won the Silver medal at the World Para Athletics Grand Prix in the men's javelin throw (F46 category). (देवेंद्र झाझरिया — रजत पदक)

• Jhajharia is India's most decorated para-athlete in the javelin throw F46 class, in which athletes have an upper-limb impairment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Paralympic record: Devendra Jhajharia won Gold at Athens 2004, Gold at Rio 2016 and Silver at Tokyo 2020 — making him the first Indian to win two Paralympic gold medals.

• Awards: Arjuna Award (2004), Padma Shri (2012), Khel Ratna (2017) and Padma Bhushan (2022).

NOTE

• Other leading Indian para-athletes: Sumit Antil (javelin F64, world record), Avani Lekhara (shooting), Mariyappan Thangavelu (high jump), Deepa Malik (shot put) and Krishna Nagar (badminton).

• Para sports in India are governed by the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI).

question: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
solution_text:
The correct answer is the cytokinesis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phragmoplast is a structure of microtubules, microfilaments and vesicles that forms between the two daughter nuclei in plant cells and guides the formation of the cell plate, which later becomes the new cell wall. This happens during cytokinesis — the division of the cytoplasm. (कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन — साइटोकाइनेसिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Karyokinesis = division of the nucleus (it takes place through prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase). Cytokinesis = division of the cytoplasm, which follows karyokinesis.

• In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the furrowing/cleavage of the cell membrane; in plant cells, by cell-plate formation (because of the rigid cell wall).

• The S phase of interphase is when DNA replication occurs; the G0 phase is the quiescent/resting phase in which a cell exits the cell cycle.

NOTE

• Cell cycle = Interphase (G1 → S → G2) + M phase (mitosis + cytokinesis).

• Mitosis produces two identical diploid daughter cells; meiosis produces four haploid cells and occurs in reproductive cells.

question: In which type of forests are Mahogany, Rosewood and Cinchona trees found in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical Evergreen forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahogany, Rosewood, Ebony and Cinchona are typical trees of India's Tropical Evergreen (rain) forests. (उष्णकटिबंधीय सदाबहार वन)

• These forests grow in areas receiving more than 200 cm of annual rainfall with a short dry season — the Western Ghats, the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the upper Assam/North-East region and the Lakshadweep group.

• As there is no definite time for the trees to shed leaves, the forests always appear green.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon) forests — the most widespread forests of India (rainfall 70–200 cm); trees such as teak, sal, sandalwood, shisham, khair, neem shed leaves for 6–8 weeks in the dry summer.

• Mangrove (Tidal/Littoral) forests — grow in coastal deltas and salt water; Sundari trees dominate the Sundarbans delta of West Bengal.

• Montane forests — found in hilly/mountainous areas; wet temperate forests, then pine, deodar, silver fir, spruce and cedar, and finally alpine grasslands.

NOTE

• Cinchona is medicinally important — the anti-malarial drug quinine is obtained from its bark.

• The Thorn and Scrub forests (rainfall below 70 cm) of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Haryana contain acacia (babool), palms, euphorbias and cacti.

question: Lebang Boomani dance is the harvest dance of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Lebang Boomani" dance is the famous harvest dance of Tripura, performed by the Tripuri tribe. (त्रिपुरा का फसल नृत्य)

• It is performed after the harvest, when the colourful "Lebang" insects visit the hill slopes; the men play bamboo clappers and flutes while the women dance to trap the insects.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Tripura: Hojagiri (by Reang women, balancing pitchers/lamps on the head), Garia, Jhum and Bizu dance.

• Folk dances of neighbouring states: Cheraw / Bamboo dance (Mizoram), Bihu (Assam), Nongkrem and Laho (Meghalaya), Bardo Chham (Arunachal Pradesh), Chang Lo/Sua Lua (Nagaland), Thang-Ta and Lai Haraoba (Manipur).

NOTE

• Tripura's capital is Agartala; its major tribes are the Tripuri, Reang, Jamatia, Chakma and Halam. Kokborok is a major language of the state.

question: Why is it important to distinguish between final and intermediate goods/services in national income accounting?
option_1: It helps in tracking changes in consumer preferences and market demand.
option_2: It helps in a more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.
option_3: It provides insight into the distribution of income among different sectors.
option_4: It helps in determining the overall quality of goods and services produced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. It helps in a more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In national income accounting (राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन) it is essential to distinguish between final goods (अंतिम वस्तुएँ) and intermediate goods (मध्यवर्ती वस्तुएँ) in order to avoid the problem of "double counting (दोहरी गणना)".

◦ Final goods are those purchased for final use by the ultimate consumer or as investment — their value is included in GDP.

◦ Intermediate goods are used up as inputs in producing other goods (e.g., flour bought by a bakery) — their value is already contained in the price of the final good, so counting them again would inflate national income.

• By excluding intermediate goods, GDP measures only the value added at each stage, giving a more accurate measure of economic growth and productivity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Three methods of measuring national income: the Value Added / Product method, the Income method and the Expenditure method — all three should give the same figure.

• Key aggregates: GDP (Gross Domestic Product), NDP = GDP – Depreciation, GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad, NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

NOTE

• The National Income Committee was set up in 1949 under P. C. Mahalanobis; the first scientific estimate of India's national income was given by Dr. V. K. R. V. Rao. Dadabhai Naoroji gave the first estimate in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".

question: Which of the following is NOT a directive principle of state policy?
option_1: Separation of the judiciary from executive
option_2: Reside in any part of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reside in any part of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The right to "reside and settle in any part of the territory of India" is a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(e), and NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy. (अनुच्छेद 19(1)(ङ) — मूल अधिकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other three options are Directive Principles (Part IV, Articles 36–51):

◦ Article 50 — Separation of the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

◦ Article 44 — a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens throughout the territory of India.

◦ Article 49 — Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.

• Directive Principles are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37). They were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland.

NOTE

• The six freedoms under Article 19(1): (a) speech and expression, (b) assemble peaceably without arms, (c) form associations/unions, (d) move freely throughout India, (e) reside and settle in any part of India, (g) practise any profession or carry on any occupation, trade or business. [Clause (f) — right to property — was deleted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.]

• Other important DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (village panchayats), Article 43B (co-operative societies), Article 45 (early childhood care), Article 47 (prohibition of intoxicating drinks), Article 48A (protection of environment and wildlife), Article 51 (promotion of international peace).

question: In which state is the Sanchi Stupa situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sanchi Stupa is situated at Sanchi in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, about 46 km from Bhopal. (सांची स्तूप — मध्य प्रदेश)

• The Great Stupa (Stupa No. 1) was originally commissioned by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE over the relics of the Buddha; it was later enlarged and the famous carved toranas (gateways) were added in the Satavahana period (1st century BCE).

• Sanchi was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A stupa is a hemispherical dome-shaped structure containing relics of the Buddha or Buddhist saints. Its parts include the Anda (dome), Harmika, Yashti/Chhatra (umbrella), Medhi, Vedika (railing) and Pradakshina Patha (circumambulatory path).

• The site was rediscovered by General Taylor in 1818; conservation was carried out under Sir John Marshall.

NOTE

• Other famous stupas: Dhamek Stupa, Sarnath (UP), Amaravati Stupa (Andhra Pradesh), Bharhut Stupa (MP), Kesariya Stupa (Bihar — the tallest) and Nagarjunakonda (Andhra Pradesh).

• Other heritage sites of Madhya Pradesh: Khajuraho temples, the Bhimbetka rock shelters, and the Rani Kamlapati/Bhojpur monuments.

question: Who is the nominal executive authority of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India (भारत का राष्ट्रपति) is the nominal / titular / de jure executive head of the country, while the Prime Minister is the real / de facto executive head.

• Under Article 53, the executive power of the Union is vested in the President, but he exercises it on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74). The 42nd and 44th Amendments made this advice binding on him (he may return it once for reconsideration).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and of Delhi and Puducherry, by the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote (Article 54–55).

• Qualifications (Article 58): a citizen of India, 35 years of age, qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, and not holding any office of profit.

• Term: 5 years; removable only by impeachment for violation of the Constitution (Article 61).

NOTE

• The Vice-President (उपराष्ट्रपति) is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64); the Attorney General (महान्यायवादी, Article 76) is the highest law officer of the Union.

• At the State level, the Governor is the nominal executive and the Chief Minister is the real executive.

question: Who among the following is the author of the book, ‘Unfinished: A Memoir’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priyanka Chopra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unfinished: A Memoir" (published in 2021) is the memoir of the Indian actress, producer and global icon Priyanka Chopra Jonas. (प्रियंका चोपड़ा की आत्मकथा)

• The book traces her childhood in India and the United States, her win at Miss World 2000, her Bollywood career and her move to Hollywood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Priyanka Chopra won the National Film Award for Best Actress for "Fashion (2008)" and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016. She starred in the American series "Quantico".

• Kareena Kapoor Khan has written "Kareena Kapoor Khan's Pregnancy Bible"; Twinkle Khanna wrote "Mrs Funnybones".

NOTE

• Other well-known Indian autobiographies/memoirs: Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), An Autobiography / The Story of My Experiments with Truth (Jawaharlal Nehru / Mahatma Gandhi), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Ace Against Odds (Sania Mirza), The Race of My Life (Milkha Singh), Straight from the Heart (Kapil Dev), Romancing with Life (Dev Anand).

question: The South China Sea is a part of which of the following oceans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The South China Sea is a marginal sea of the western Pacific Ocean, lying between mainland South-East Asia and the islands of Taiwan, the Philippines and Borneo. (दक्षिण चीन सागर — प्रशांत महासागर का भाग)

• It is bordered by China, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore and Vietnam, and connects to the Indian Ocean through the Strait of Malacca.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The South China Sea is one of the world's busiest shipping routes, carrying about a third of global maritime trade, and is rich in oil, natural gas and fisheries.

• It is a major geopolitical flashpoint, with disputes over the Spratly Islands, the Paracel Islands and the Scarborough Shoal, and over China's "Nine-Dash Line" claim, which was rejected by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 2016.

NOTE

• The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean; the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) in it is the deepest point on earth (~11,000 m).

• The five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern (Antarctic) and Arctic. Other marginal seas of the Pacific: the East China Sea, the Yellow Sea, the Sea of Japan, the Bering Sea and the Coral Sea.

question: The official language of which neighbouring country of India is ‘Dhivehi'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maldives.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dhivehi" (also called Maldivian) is the official language of the Maldives, an island nation in the Indian Ocean and India's maritime neighbour. (मालदीव की राजभाषा — धिवेही)

• Dhivehi is an Indo-Aryan language, closely related to Sinhala, and is written in the Thaana script, which is written from right to left.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Maldives: capital Malé; currency Maldivian Rufiyaa; it is the smallest Asian country by land area and population, made up of about 1,190 coral islands in 26 atolls.

• India–Maldives cooperation includes Operation Cactus (1988) and the joint exercise "Ekuverin".

NOTE

• Official languages of India's neighbours: Sri Lanka — Sinhala and Tamil; Bhutan — Dzongkha; China — Mandarin (Standard Chinese); Nepal — Nepali; Bangladesh — Bengali; Pakistan — Urdu (and English); Myanmar — Burmese; Afghanistan — Pashto and Dari.

question: Under which scheme of Airport Authority of India did the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor inaugurate UMEED Market Place at Srinagar international airport for supporting local art and artisans of Self Help Groups of J&K Rural Livelihood Mission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AVSAR Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "UMEED Market Place" at Srinagar International Airport was inaugurated by the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir under the AVSAR scheme of the Airports Authority of India (AAI). (अवसर योजना — भारतीय विमानपत्तन प्राधिकरण)

• AVSAR stands for "Airport as Venue for Skilled Artisans of Region". Under it, the AAI provides space free of cost at its airports to Self Help Groups (SHGs) to display and sell local handicrafts and products.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "UMEED" is the J&K Rural Livelihood Mission (the state's version of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission), which works to empower rural women through Self Help Groups.

• The AAI generally allots 100–200 sq ft of space at each airport terminal on a rotational basis under the AVSAR scheme, giving artisans access to a large customer base.

NOTE

• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) was constituted in 1995 under the Ministry of Civil Aviation; it manages more than 130 airports in the country.

• Other civil-aviation schemes: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (2016), and Krishi UDAN for the air transport of perishable agricultural produce.

question: Who was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi and took away an immense amount of wealth in 1739?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nadir Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nadir Shah, the ruler of Persia (Iran), invaded India and defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah "Rangeela" in the Battle of Karnal (February 1739). He then entered Delhi, ordered a general massacre (qatl-e-aam) and carried away immense wealth, including the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus) of Shah Jahan. (नादिर शाह — 1739, दिल्ली पर आक्रमण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nadir Shah's invasion exposed the weakness of the Mughal Empire and hastened its decline; the Mughals also ceded all territories west of the Indus.

• Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) of Afghanistan invaded India several times between 1748 and 1767 and defeated the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761).

• Abbas I (Shah Abbas the Great) was a famous Safavid ruler of Persia (1588–1629) who captured Kandahar from the Mughals.

NOTE

• Sequence of foreign invasions: Alexander (326 BCE) → Mahmud of Ghazni (1000–1027) → Muhammad Ghori (1175–1206) → Timur (1398) → Babur (1526) → Nadir Shah (1739) → Ahmad Shah Abdali (1748–1767).

question: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi belonged to the __________ Gharana.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (1922–2011) was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist who belonged to the Kirana Gharana. (पंडित भीमसेन जोशी — किराना घराना)

• He was a disciple of Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar), himself a disciple of Ustad Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of the Kirana Gharana. Bhimsen Joshi was celebrated for his khayal singing and for devotional abhangs and bhajans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008 — the highest civilian honour — along with the Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1985), Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• He famously sang in the national-integration video "Mile Sur Mera Tumhara".

NOTE

• Major Hindustani gharanas: Kirana (Abdul Karim Khan, Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal), Gwalior (the oldest khayal gharana), Agra, Jaipur–Atrauli (Kesarbai Kerkar), Patiala (Bade Ghulam Ali Khan), Rampur–Sahaswan and Banaras (famous for thumri and tabla).

• Hindustani music prevails in North India; Carnatic music is the classical tradition of South India.

question: Mahari Dance and Gotipua Dance belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both the Mahari dance and the Gotipua dance belong to Odisha, and are the two traditional streams from which the classical dance Odissi developed. (ओडिशा — महरी और गोटीपुआ नृत्य)

◦ Mahari — performed by the Maharis (devadasis), the temple dancers of the Jagannath Temple, Puri, as a ritual offering to the deity.

◦ Gotipua — performed by young boys dressed as girls outside the temple; "goti" = single and "pua" = boy. It involves acrobatic bandha nritya postures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Odissi is one of the eight classical dances of India and is known for its tribhangi (three-bend) posture and the chauka stance representing Lord Jagannath.

• Famous Odissi exponents: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sonal Mansingh, Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Deba Prasad Das.

• Odisha's folk dances include Chhau (Mayurbhanj), Ghumura, Ranapa, Dalkhai and Sambalpuri.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Identify the WRONG pair of dancer and the related dance form from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumkum Dhar - Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The wrongly matched pair is "Kumkum Dhar – Kuchipudi". Kumkum Dhar is a distinguished exponent of Kathak (of the Lucknow gharana), not Kuchipudi. She was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathak. (कुमकुम धर — कथक, न कि कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other three pairs are correctly matched:

◦ Meenakshi Chitharanjan – Bharatanatyam: a leading Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style from Chennai.

◦ Sruti Bandopadhay – Manipuri: a well-known Manipuri dancer, scholar and teacher from West Bengal.

◦ Trilochan Mohanta – Chhau: an exponent of the Mayurbhanj Chhau dance of Odisha.

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India, marked by fast footwork (tatkar), pirouettes (chakkars) and storytelling; its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, famous for the tarangam (dancing on the rim of a brass plate).

• Chhau is a semi-classical masked dance of Odisha (Mayurbhanj), Jharkhand (Seraikella) and West Bengal (Purulia), inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

question: Which of the following musicians is popularly known as ‘Panchamda’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RD Burman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Hindi film music director Rahul Dev Burman (R. D. Burman, 1939–1994) was popularly known as "Panchamda". (पंचमदा — आर. डी. बर्मन)

• The nickname "Pancham" is said to have come either because as a baby he cried in the fifth note ("pa" — the pancham swar) or because the actor Ashok Kumar remarked that his cry sounded like the note "Pa".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He was the son of the composer Sachin Dev Burman (S. D. Burman) and was married to the singer Asha Bhosle.

• He revolutionised Hindi film music in the 1970s–80s with films such as Sholay, Amar Prem, Hare Rama Hare Krishna, Yaadon Ki Baaraat, Teesri Manzil, Caravan and 1942: A Love Story (for which he won a posthumous Filmfare Award).

NOTE

• Other great Hindi film composers: Naushad (Mughal-e-Azam, Baiju Bawra — Dadasaheb Phalke Award 1992), Khayyam (Umrao Jaan, Kabhi Kabhie), Ravi (Chaudhvin Ka Chand, Gharana), Madan Mohan, Shankar–Jaikishan, Laxmikant–Pyarelal and A. R. Rahman.

question: The ‘Mukteshwar’ dance festival is held from 14th to 16th January at the Mukteshwar temple in the state of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mukteshwar Dance Festival" is held every year from 14th to 16th January in the courtyard of the Mukteshwar Temple at Bhubaneswar, Odisha. (मुक्तेश्वर नृत्य महोत्सव — ओडिशा)

• It is organised by the Odisha Tourism Department and is devoted mainly to Odissi dance, performed against the backdrop of the 10th-century temple.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Mukteshwar Temple (c. 950–975 CE) is a Kalinga-style Shiva temple famous for its exquisitely carved torana (arched gateway); it is called the "Gem of Odisha architecture".

• Bhubaneswar is known as the "Temple City of India"; other famous temples there are the Lingaraja, Rajarani and Parashurameswara temples.

NOTE

• Other dance festivals of Odisha: the Konark Dance Festival (December, at Konark) and the Rajarani Music Festival (January, Bhubaneswar).

• Major festivals of Odisha: the Rath Yatra of Puri, Raja Parba, Nuakhai and the Bali Jatra at Cuttack.

question: Select from among the given options the autobiography of Milkha Singh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Race of My Life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Race of My Life" is the autobiography of the legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh, co-written with his daughter Sonia Sanwalka and published in 2013. (मिल्खा सिंह की आत्मकथा)

• The Bollywood film "Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (2013)" was based on this book.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Milkha Singh, called "The Flying Sikh", won gold in the 400 m at the 1958 Commonwealth Games (Cardiff) — India's first athletics gold there — and at the 1958 and 1962 Asian Games. He famously finished fourth in the 400 m final at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1959.

NOTE

• The other options: "A Shot at History" — Abhinav Bindra (India's first individual Olympic gold medallist, shooting, Beijing 2008); "The Test of My Life" — Yuvraj Singh; "One Life Is Not Enough" — K. Natwar Singh.
